_comment: File-discovery eval cases (Defect A + B). Raj's tester reported 'I couldn't find any files in that folder' and only got results after pasting an absolute path. These cases stage a real file at a real location and assert resolveReadablePath() finds it — or refuses it, for the sandbox rows. `layout` describes where the file goes relative to $HOME; the runner creates and removes it.

cases.why: Windows OneDrive Known Folder Move puts the real Desktop at %USERPROFILE%\OneDrive\Desktop. Every Ministry laptop with KFM has this shape; a ~/Desktop-only probe misses all of it.
The exact path Raj's tester used: C:\Users\camer\OneDrive\Desktop\MoE Agent Testing Folder.
Work/school accounts use 'OneDrive - <Tenant>'. A live MoE laptop signed in as @moe.gov.tt gets this folder name, not plain 'OneDrive'.
Two levels below a business-OneDrive Desktop — within the 3-deep scan budget. Principals nest by term and topic.
The non-KFM baseline must not regress while fixing KFM.
Raj's P2 and P4 both write into an Output_Files folder, then need to read it back.
The workaround Raj's tester fell back to must keep working.
~/ prefix is what the agent itself emits when it echoes a path back.

Defect B: the guard's own message says 'or tmp directory are allowed', and renderer file:stage outputs briefly live there. os.tmpdir() on macOS is under /var/folders which is itself a symlink to /private/var.
Defect B proper: /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp on macOS. The candidate was realpath-resolved but the roots were not, so startsWith() failed and the guard refused a path it claimed to allow.
The KFM widening must NOT widen the sandbox. Exists on macOS and Linux, so a 'not found' pass would be a false negative.
The not-found message must enumerate what was searched — that is what turns 'I couldn't find any files' into something a principal can act on.
